title: Support the WebSocket Denial Response ASGI extension
description:
uvicorn now can return a response from websocket apps that choose to reject a connection with a custom response.
See https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/2041/files for related work.

This is a re-submission of pr #1907

comments.author: Kludex
comments.body:
Interesting... I've just found this:

> The protocol server must not start sending the response to the client until it has received at least one Response Body event.

Ref.: https://asgi.readthedocs.io/en/latest/specs/www.html#response-start-send-event

Meaning that we shouldn't be sending the 404 if nobody is provided... But that also means that we have an issue with the HTTP implementations :thinking:

comments.author: kristjanvalur
comments.body:
> Meaning that we shouldn't be sending the 404 if nobody is provided... But that also means that we have an issue with the HTTP implementations 🤔

Yes, h11 definitely starts sending the header before receiving the first body.

This can be fixed, I can fix both h11 and websockets to wait for the first body...    I can do it for websockets in this PR and then a followup one for h11_impl.py

review_comments.author: kristjanvalur
review_comments.body:
This is similar to the code in http/h11_impl.py, e.g.
```python
        except BaseException as exc:
            msg = "Exception in ASGI application\n"
            self.logger.error(msg, exc_info=exc)
            if not self.response_started:
                await self.send_500_response()
            else:
                self.transport.close()
```
If an attempt is made to send a 500_response() after the sending of a response has already begun, then the application fails in a nasty way.  send_500_response() fails in a way which isn't caught, no error is output or anything.  This is what was causing me to comment this:

```
I am unable to silence the wsproto internal error which happens when it is trying to send a 500 error.

wsproto will start a response as soon as it gets the .start message
It then gets an invalid message and attempts to send a 500 response
but it cannot because it has already started a response.
An exception is not raised via the async send() method but somewhere else which I cannot fully understand, so the test fails.
I've added a skip for the WSProto case, but maybe there is a better solution? Skipping is not ideal, because this test was designed to increase coverage.
```

We could of course try to fix that error, it is bad if an internal exception is hard to debug, but that's not within the scope of this PR.  
I guess the check could be moved into `send_500_response()` but I was following the style of `h11_impl.py`

review_comments.author: kristjanvalur
review_comments.body: If you approve, I´ll move this check into `send_500_response()` where it properly belongs, along with a comment, and do the same in h11_impl.py for consistency.  We can also log the situation.

review_comments.author: Kludex
review_comments.body: It makes sense for WebSockets to add the `content-length`, since we can't have a chunked one there.

review_comments.author: kristjanvalur
review_comments.body: well, this is only about what happens if the app doesn't provide a content-length and only provides the raw body data.  the defaults for these two protocols are different.  Technically, you _can_ provide chunked data over the websockets:  The app, provides the "chunked" header, and then provides the chunks, with the appropriate chunk headers (as an application should do if it provides that header (I think).  I think that nowadays it is rare for an application to specify content length or transfer encoding...

review_comments.author: kristjanvalur
review_comments.body: If you say so :), We didn't have those fancy type decorations in the old days.

review_comments.author: kristjanvalur
review_comments.body:
I know.  I disagree, I think the _recommendation_  is a good one because it enlarges the window during which the server can still send a 500 error in case the application messes up.  It is not a requirement but (IMHO) good practice in a library, and that is the reason I wrote the code that way.
But it is your call of course, happy to get this merged either way.

review_comments.author: Kludex
review_comments.body: I understand, and it makes sense... But I'll rather not have a mismatch in how the HTTP implementations behave, and the WebSockets.
